sketch.skeleton: a flat hand-drawn black-line sketch of a {subject} on a pure white background, {register}, {framing}, {treatment}, {linework}, {annotation}, the entire image is white space with the drawing centered — at least 60 percent of the image is plain white, no shading, no fill, no gradients, no shadows, no color besides the black ink and white field, NOT a 3D render, NOT a CAD drawing, NOT a clean technical illustration, NOT a photograph of the actual object — this is a designer's small playful working sketch in the spirit of nendo's process diagrams and gestural shape-first studies, hand-drawn with real pen-pressure roughness, the gesture and the approach are what matter, the line itself is the entire image

register: nendo minimal-process register: small considered drawing floating in vast white, single confident contour, hand-drawn roughness, the gesture is the entire piece

shape-first chunky-contour register: the object built from primitive geometry (cylinders, circles, rectangles, ovals) stacked or joined together, bold thick black outline, pure silhouette construction with no interior detail, confident kindergarten-clear shapes, no shading, no fill

iPad / digital-thumbnail-sheet register: a sheet of multiple small confident black-ink gestural sketches of the object scattered across the frame, exploring different angles, configurations, and component studies, mid-design energy, like a designer's iPad scratch page
process-diagram register: a small numbered or arrowed sequence of the same object across two to four steps, each step a tiny drawing with a small ALL-CAPS one-word handwritten label below it
loose gestural register: dense flowing ink, the object built from continuous overlapping squiggles and quick contour passes, calligraphic energy, single confident gesture
shape-block register: the object reduced to a few large simple rectangular and circular masses with no detail, stacked or joined, almost iconic
framing: the drawing occupies roughly 25 percent of the frame, centered, with vast empty white space on every side
the drawing is small and floats in the center, more than 75 percent of the image is plain white
a tiny drawing in the lower-center of the frame with a wide expanse of empty white above
the drawing slightly off-center, generous white margins on all four sides
the drawing fits within the central third of the frame, the rest is pure white
the drawing in the upper-third of the frame with empty white below for breathing room
the studies arranged across the frame with deliberate empty space between them
treatment: the object alone as a single one-pass drawing, no other elements
the object alone, isometric three-quarter view, faint construction lines beneath the contour
the object alone in pure profile / side elevation, a single confident silhouette
the object alone in plan view from above, simple geometric construction
the object plus a tiny stick-figure character beside it for scale, sometimes with a small thought-bubble
an orthographic pair — small front-elevation and side-elevation of the object placed side by side on white
an exploded view — components pulled apart along thin guide axes with hairline arrows showing how they fit
a cross-section / cutaway showing the inside of the object, exterior outline plus interior lines
a scale-comparison study — the object drawn twice side by side at different sizes
a thumbnail page — three to six very small rough versions of the object from slightly different angles arranged across the white
the object with one curved arrow showing motion or rotation around an axis
the object with one or two thin pointer lines and one-word handwritten labels calling out features
an action sketch — the object mid-use, a hand or finger lightly suggested at the edge in the same line weight
an alternate-form study — two or three small variations of the object's silhouette stacked or arranged together
the object with light dimension marks at its edges (e.g. 190, 280) in the same hand
a 2-step or 3-step process diagram — small drawings connected by thin arrows, tiny ALL-CAPS one-word labels below each
a component-study sheet — the object plus a few of its key parts drawn small and separate around it

bold thick black contour line, even weight, confident closed shapes, almost marker-like — pairs naturally with the shape-first register
thin steady black ink with small overlaps at intersections, working-drawing energy, never perfectly straight — pairs naturally with iPad-sheet and thumbnail registers
